<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par54 />''affect'' to be of a certain character. E.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַּדֵּל|translate=to make oneself great, to act proudly}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַכֵּם|translate=to show oneself wise, crafty}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַלָּה|translate=to pretend to be ill}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעַשֵּׁר|translate=to make}}, i.e. ''to feign oneself rich''; {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׂתָּרֵר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=13}}, ''to make oneself a prince''; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַבֵּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=10}}, ''to act in an excited manner like a prophet, to rave''. The meaning of {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} sometimes coincides with that of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, both forms being in use together, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָבַל|translate=to mourn}}, in Qal only in poetic style, in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} in prose. On the accusative after Hithpaʿēl (regarded as a transitive verb), see {{GHGpar|117|w}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|f}}
(''b'') It expresses ''reciprocal'' action, like {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|d}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְרָאָה|translate=to look upon one another}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=41|verse=8}}; —but

(''c'') It more often indicates an action less directly affecting the subject, and describes it as performed ''with regard to'' or ''for'' oneself, in one’s own special interest (cf. {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|e}}). Hithpaʿēl in such cases readily takes an accusative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפָּרֵק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=3}} and {{GHGheb|text=הִתְנַצֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=6}} ''to tear off from oneself''; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפַּשֵּׁט|translate=exuit sibi}} (''vestem''), {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפַּתַּח|translate=solvit sibi}} (''vincula''); {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַיֵּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=12}}, ''to take'' (''something'') ''as one’s provision''; without an accusative, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְהַלֵּךְ|translate=to walk about for oneself}} (''ambulare''); {{GHGheb|text=הִתְפַּלֵּל|translate=sibi intercedere}} (see Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=15}}); {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַקָּה|translate=to draw a line for oneself}}, Job {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=27|hidebook=1}}; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=14|verse=2}}, see § 57, note.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|g}}
(''d'') Only seldom is it {{GHGterm|passive}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִיא תִתְהַלָּֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=30}} ''she shall be praised''; {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁתַּכַּח|translate=to be forgotten}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=10}}, where the reflexive sense (''to bring oneself into oblivion'') has altogether disappeared. Cf. Niphʿal, {{GHGpar|51|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|h}}
The passive form {{GHGterm|Hothpaʿal}} is found only in the few following examples: {{GHGheb|text=הֻטַּמָּא|translate=to be defiled}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=4}}; {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻכַּבֵּס|translate=to be washed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=55.56}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֻדַּ֫שְׁנָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הֻתְדַּשְׁנָה}}, the {{GHGheb|text=נָה}} being treated as if it were the afformative of the ''fem. plur.'') ''it is made fat'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=6}}. On {{GHGheb|text=הָתְפָּֽקְדוּ}}, see l.

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|i}}
Denominatives with a reflexive meaning are {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַהֵד|translate=to embrace Judaism}}, from {{GHGheb|text=(יְהוּדָה) יְהוּד|translate=Judah}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַיֵּד|translate=to provision oneself for a journey}}, from {{GHGheb|text=צֵידָה|translate=provision for a journey}} (see {{GHGpar|72|m}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|54|k}}
Rem. 1. As in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, so in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the perfect very frequently (in stems ending in {{GHGheb|text=ג}}, {{GHGheb|text=ק}}, {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=פ}}) has retained the original {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the final syllable (while in the ordinary form it is attenuated, as in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, to ''ĭ'' and then lengthened to ''ē''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְאַנַּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=21}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=13|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=15|verse=8|hidebook=1}}; with {{GHGheb|text=וְ|translate=consecutive}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=21}}; so also in the imperfect and imperative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְחַכַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=16}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=8.18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=10|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=58|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְחַזַּק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=5|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶֽתְאַפַּק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=12}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=44}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=7|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=38|verse=23}}, ''ĭ'' takes the place of ''ă'' in the final syllable of the stem before {{GHGheb|text=שׁ}} (cf. {{GHGpar|44|d}}), and in the last passage before {{GHGheb|text=ל}}. In the ''perfect, imperfect'' (with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=16}}), and {{GHGterm|imperative}} of {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} (as well as of ''Hithpô‛ēl, Hithpa‛lēl, Hithpalpēl'', § 55) the original ''ă'' always returns in {{GHGterm|pause}} as {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְאַזָּרָ֑}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=93|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְאַבָּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְהַלָּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִתְלַכָּֽדוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=30|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=5}} and {{GHGpar|74|b}}.—The ''ā'' also appears before the fuller ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} in the plural of the imperfect (cf. {{GHGpar|47|m}}) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=9}}, Jb<section end=par54 /><noinclude>
